title: Regional fallback queue coupling and circuit backoff review
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-28 a customer-driven traffic spike caused a cascade during cross-region failover: the secondary region's circuit breakers and priority queues saturated, backlog coupling between priority tiers amplified latency, and automated load-shedding evicted some high-priority routed requests. Result: widespread SLO misses for 99th-percentile tail latency for ~22 minutes across the affected customers and visible errors for a subset of enterprise customers.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2026-02-28 15:11 UTC: Primary (us-west-2) experienced token surge from a single high-throughput customer (unexpected workload pattern).
- 15:12 UTC: Smart routing triggered cross-region fallback to us-east-1 per policy because primary latency exceeded SLO thresholds.
- 15:12–15:20 UTC: Secondary region saw rapid fanout; circuit breakers tripped open under surge, but breaker hysteresis was long (2m) and re-open decisions allowed repeated short exposures.
- 15:13–15:25 UTC: Priority-queue coupling caused lower-priority backlog to crowd out urgent work due to shared token bucket accounting; KV cache cold starts in the secondary region amplified tail latency.
- 15:18 UTC: Load-shedding policy started evicting requests based on estimated cost heuristics; misclassification and duplication from client-side retries caused some high-priority requests to be shed.
- 15:33 UTC: Manual routing rollback to primary and emergency circuit-threshold adjustment reduced new fanout; by 15:43 UTC recovery observed and SLOs returned to baseline.

Impact:
- Duration: 22 minutes of elevated 99p latency and errors; some enterprise customers observed degraded responses and higher error rates.
- SLOs: 99p latency SLO for the host model group missed by up to 2x during the window.
- Billing/Cost: transient increase in cross-region egress and emergency scale-ups; minor cost impact.

Root cause summary: The orchestration allowed an immediate full-fanout failover without staged ramping. Secondary-region protective systems (circuit breakers and priority queues) were configured with hysteresis and shared token accounting that amplified backlog instead of isolating it. Cold KV caches and a mismatch between retry/dedup heuristics caused request duplication. The combined effect caused cascade saturation and the load-shedding policy to evict some high-priority traffic, producing SLO misses.
root_cause_summary: Immediate full-fanout cross-region failover combined with long circuit-breaker hysteresis, shared priority token accounting, KV cold-starts, and retry duplication led to backlog amplification and incorrect load-shedding of high-priority requests.
contributing_factors: Failover orchestration had no staged ramp/rate-limit for cross-region traffic
Circuit breaker hysteresis window (2 minutes) too long for short surges
Priority queue token bucket was shared/undifferentiated across tiers leading to coupling
KV cache cold-starts in secondary region increased per-request latency
Client retry loops caused duplicate requests that exacerbated load
Monitoring alarms aggregated region-level signals and missed per-priority queue depth early warning
mitigations_during_incident: Manually updated routing policy to reduce fanout to us-east-1
Temporarily increased circuit breaker thresholds in the secondary region to avoid immediate open/close churn
Disabled non-critical background batching for 12 minutes to free up queue slots
Triggered manual cache warm-up for the hot model prefixes
Applied temporary suppression of client-side aggressive retry guidance via status code 429 with retry-after headers
permanent_actions: Introduce staged ramp for cross-region failover: soft-ramp (10%), then 30s observation, then 100% if healthy — owner: Jordan Lee — due: 2026-03-29
Isolate token buckets per-priority and enforce hard reservation for high-priority tier — owner: Maya Chen — due: 2026-03-24
Reduce circuit-breaker hysteresis and add surge dampening backoff with exponential cool-down to prevent oscillation — owner: Priya Nambiar — due: 2026-03-31
Implement KV cache warm-prioritization: on failover trigger, prefetch top 100 hot prefixes for models deployed in target region — owner: Samir Gupta — due: 2026-03-18
Add dedup-by-request-id in the front door for a 30s window to stop retry amplification — owner: Lina Rodriguez — due: 2026-03-20
Create per-priority SLO dashboards and queue-depth alerts in Datadog (99p latency by priority) — owner: Observability Team — due: 2026-03-17
Update failover runbook to include rollback step and checklist for circuit adjustments — owner: Oncall Runbook Team — due: 2026-03-15
